stem: A bar chart shows the quarterly sales (in Rs lakhs) of a company: Q1 = 40, Q2 = 55, Q3 = 50, Q4 = 60. What is the total sales represented by the bar chart?

per_option_rationale.rationale: 40 + 55 + 50 + 60 = 205, not 200; this slip drops 5 from the sum.
165 = 40 + 55 + 50 + 20; the Q4 value was misread as 20 instead of 60.
210 = 205 + 5; an addition slip that adds an extra 5.

explanation: Reading each bar value and summing: 40 + 55 + 50 + 60 = 205 lakhs. Bar charts allow totals by summation; the bars do not themselves indicate a total.

explanation_sections.punchline: Summing individual bar values 40 + 55 + 50 + 60 = 205 lakhs is the only operation needed.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: bar chart represents discrete category values. Sum all category values to obtain the aggregate total.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always verify each bar value before summing; a misread bar is the most common error in diagram reading.
explanation_sections.timing: 50 s. Simply add the four values; eliminate options 1 and 4 by noting 40+60=100 and 55+50=105, total = 205.
